atomicity.reason: Two shall-clauses, raise below 5 °C and withdraw at 10 °C or above; they are facets of one hysteresis behaviour but separately testable, and the title states only the raise.
atomicity.suggestion: Split into a raise and a withdraw requirement, or state one hysteresis requirement ('raised below 5 °C, held until 10 °C or above') in both title and body.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: both thresholds, the input (lowest valid cell temperature), the output (heating request on the thermal interface) and the purpose (restoring charging power on a cold morning) are in the body.

feasibility.reason: A two-threshold comparator on cell temperature is routine and contradicts nothing in the linked context.

parent_fit.reason: Implements the parent's cold-morning behaviour: the pack calls for heating while its coldest cell is too cold to charge quickly and stops once that cell has warmed up.

unambiguity.reason: One reading: raise strictly below 5 °C, withdraw at 10 °C or above, request held in between.

verifiability.reason: Concrete threshold test: a lowest valid cell temperature of 4.9 °C raises the request, 9 °C keeps it, 10 °C withdraws it; thresholds, units and inclusive/exclusive limits are stated.

summary: Precise, testable hysteresis requirement; atomicity reduced because raising and withdrawing the request are bundled.
